VENTURA Prov•neal Administrator Provnneal Government of Tarlac Dear Mr. Ventura: This has reference to your letteri requesting for the Department's legal opinion on the propnety of the permanent closure of a portion of a city road without any supporting Sanggunian Ordinance. As narrated, the City Government of Tarlac, upon the directive of its Local Chief Executive, ordered the closure of a portion of Rizal Street in Barangay Poblacion in 2019. The purpose of the closure was to convert the area into an exclusive parking space for City Hall officials, employees, and visitors. As a result, the normal traffic flow in the area was significantly disrupted, prompting the implementation of a re-routing scheme. upon inquiry, the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Tarlac issued a Certification stating that no ordinance had been enacted authorizing such closure. In this regard, you raised the following questions: I. Vhether a City Government, upon instruction of its Local Chief Executive order a permanent/long time closure of a portion of a road without an ordinance; and 2. Whether a portion Of a city road may be closed to be utilized as a parking lot of city hall employees. We discuss. The authonty of local government units (LGUs) to open or close roads is expressly governed by Section 21 of Republic Act No. 7160. otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 , which provides: Section 21. Closure and Opening of Roads. — (a) A local government unit may. pursuant to an ordinance. permanently temporarily close or open anv IQcal road. alley, park. or square fallinq within lunsdiqtiqn. Provided, however, that in case of permanent closure, such ordinance must be approved by at least two-thirds (2/3) of all the members of the sanggunian, and when necessary, an adequate substitute for the public facility that is subject to closure is provided. xxx xxx xxx (c) An national or local road alle ark ors uare ma be tem oraril closed during an actual emergency. or fiesta celebrations, public rallies. agricultural or industrial fairs. or an undertaking of public works and hiqhways. telecommunications, and waterworks projects. the duration of which shall be specified by the local chief executive concerned in a written order: Provided, however, That no national or local road, alley, park, or square shall be temporarily closed for athletic, cultural, or civic activities not officially sponsored, recognized, or approved by the local government unit concemed. xxx xxx xxx The law also allows temporary closure of roads for specified purposes, such as emergencies or public events, subject to certain limitations and requirements under paragraph (c) of the same section. Based on the foregoing provision, it is unequivocally required that both temporary and permanent closure of local roads must be authorized by an ordinance enacted by the appropriate sanggunian. For permanent closure, the law specifically mandates a two- thirds vote of all its members. Accordingly, the unilateral action of the Local Chief Executive to permanently close a portion of a city road—absent any supporting ordinance—is not legally permissible. The conversion of a public road into an exclusive-use parking area for government employees constitutes a substantial deviation from its intended public use and thus demands legislative approval. Public roads are properties of the public domain held in trust by the government for the benefit of all, and their use may not be altered without due process and proper legal authority. In this case, the Certification from the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Tarlac attesting to the non-existence of an enabling ordinance confirms the absence of legal authority. Hence, the continued closure and repurposing of the road segment is considered ultra vires, and may expose the City Government and its officials to administrative, civil, or even criminal liability, should a complaint be raised. The same may also be subject to nullification by proper judicial or oversight authorities. In light of the above, it is the opinion of this Department that: I. A city road cannot be permanently or even temporarily closed—especially for exclusive use—without an ordinance duly enacted by the Sangguniang Panlungsod; and 2. The use of such public road as a parking area for City Hall employees, in the absence of such ordinance, is unauthorized and constitutes an improper use of public property. This opinion is issued without prejudice to any contrary determination by competent authorities or the courts. Page 2 of3
